title.narrative: Enhancing capacities to assess progress on water-related ecosystems (SDG 6.6.1) and on social inclusion and equality through a river basin approach

description.narrative:
The overall objective of this project is to enhance the capacities of Member States within CODIA to assess (a) progress on water-related ecosystems (SDG 6.6.1) and (b) advances in social inclusion, equality and women’s empowerment by using an integrative watershed approach. The project will build on the collaboration project between MITECO/AECID and UNESCO World Water Assessment Programme (WWAP) “Developing capacity for gender-transformative water policies and plans under climate uncertainties and risks - South America” (April 2023-December 2024), which aimed at strengthening national capacities to integrate a gender perspective into water resources management in South America.
Specifically, UNESCO WWAP in partnership IHP, proposes to undertake: a) An assessment of SDG 6.6.1 progress in the region including an integratory analysis of key interrelated governance outcomes (access, livelihoods, protection, restoration) in LAC region through illustrative country examples (desk review and analysis of selected case studies). b) A specialized training activity at the sub-basin level in selected CODIA country/ies for introducing the WWAP Integration and Equality Approach for Water Management to key basin managers, including governmental and local administration representatives, water users´ associations, conservation organizations, representatives of private sector, among others. The training will focus on the integration of the WWAP approach at a river basin level in a context of ecosystem and water use’s competition as per results of the desk review described in point a). c) Analysis of the participation of women in river basin governance by implementing selected WWAP indicators in CODIA countries. This activity will include an online survey. Preliminary, a sub-basin in the Amazon River Basin will be selected. Key partner for the sub-basin selection and implementation will be the Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization (ACTO). UNESCO has a long-standing commitment to advancing sustainable development across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), particularly by supporting research and education in natural sciences and management. Through its Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme – now in its ninth phase- UNESCO promotes an integrated and interdisciplinary approach to watershed and aquifer management. The program fosters international research in hydrology and freshwater sciences while emphasizing the social aspects of water resources. Its goal is to contribute meaningfully to SDG 6 along, as well as other global frameworks, including the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, Paris Agreement on Climate Change and the New Urban Agenda
